name: Toby, Beastie Befriender
oracle_text:
When Toby enters, create a 4/4 white Beast creature token with "This token can't attack or block alone."
As long as you control four or more creature tokens, creature tokens you control have flying.
blocked_sentences: When Toby enters, create a 4/4 white Beast creature token with "This token can't attack or block alone."

needs.what: A pair of combat restrictions judged on the *whole* declaration rather than per creature: an attacker may not be declared if it would be the only attacker its controller declares, and a blocker may not be declared if it would be the only creature its controller declares as a blocker (509.1b/508.1c -- the declaration is illegal as a whole, so it is not a per-creature prohibition and not a per-pair one). Concretely: a `cant_attack`/`cant_block` variant carrying an `alone: true` (or `min_others: 1`) flag, plus the missing enforcement point on the attack side -- an `attacks_valid(state, player)` mirroring `combat.blocks_valid`, checked where `finish_attackers` locks the declaration in and offered back through `legal_attackers`/`add_attacker` so legality never offers an attack the engine then refuses.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cant_attack` and `cant_block` are the two nearest statics and both are absolute: `characteristics.attack_forbidden`/`block_forbidden` take a single `oid` and answer yes/no with no view of the rest of the declaration, so either one here would forbid the token from ever attacking or blocking -- strictly stronger than what is printed, and invisible on screen. `block_restriction` does see more of the board but is scoped to the attacker being blocked: its `blockers` filter is a static filter over one would-be blocker (printed characteristics only), and its `require_all` flag -- the one whole-declaration check that exists (`combat._all_blockers_present`, Tromokratis) -- asks about the creatures the *defending player controls*, not about how many of them are blocking alongside this one, and lives on the attacker rather than the restricted creature. On the attack side there is no whole-declaration hook at all: `blocks_valid` exists for menace and `require_all`, but `finish_attackers` performs no equivalent validation, so even a correctly-shaped static would have nowhere to be enforced. `banding` is in the keyword list and is a different rule (damage assignment and band formation), not a co-attacker requirement.
needs.note: The second printed line -- "As long as you control four or more creature tokens, creature tokens you control have flying" -- IS expressible today (a `grant_keyword` static filtered `{"controller": "you", "is_token": true, "types": ["Creature"]}` under a `cmp` condition on a `count` of the same), so this card needs nothing new for it. Per the brief, a partly expressible card is filed whole rather than half-authored.

needs.what: A token definition for the 4/4 white Beast this card creates, carrying its own printed ability -- id along the lines of `beast_4_4_w_cant_attack_or_block_alone`, `{"types": ["Creature"], "subtypes": ["Beast"], "power": 4, "toughness": 4, "colors": ["W"], "color_identity": ["W"], "is_token": true}` plus a `kind: "static"` ability implementing the restriction above. It cannot be added until that static exists, which is why the two needs are one work item and not two.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The token pool in `data/cards/tokens.cards.json` has no white 4/4 Beast: `beast_4_4_g` and `beast_3_3_g` are green and abilityless, `cat_beast_2_2_w` is white but a 2/2 with the wrong subtype line, and `angel_4_4_w_flying_vigilance` is the only white 4/4 (wrong creature type, and it has flying and vigilance the Beast does not). `create_token` takes a fixed `def_id` and there is no way to spell out a token's characteristics inline or to bolt an ability onto an existing definition at creation time, so substituting any of them would silently print a different card. Tokens do support abilities (clue_token, treasure_token, junk_token and four others carry `abilities`), so the definition itself is only blocked on the missing static effect, not on the token format. Verified against the gates: an invented id is refused by the registry gate ("create_token references unknown card 'beast_4_4_w_cant_attack_or_block_alone'"), while substituting `beast_4_4_g` *loads and passes the text gates* -- it would ship a green abilityless 4/4 under Toby's printed white Beast line with nothing to flag it, which is exactly the silent-approximation failure this record exists to avoid. Dropping the line instead is caught by the residual gate ("printed text not represented").
